items.title: Konitz Lee — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Larry turned around and said: “He can push it in or pull it out but don’t leave it were it is”.

ctx.x: With the Metropole Orchestra. Oh, the piece that he wrote for me he called “A Personal Voice” and the fact is, I think, that’s part of the character of my sound: up on the line of the pitch, or over sometimes. I lived with that positively and negatively over the years, but that’s it. When I sat at the Village Vanguard one time at the bar, Cedar Walton played as a trio and then called Jackie McLean up. Larry Willis was sitting in front of me at the bar and Jackie was really sharp.
